title: Cell Sorting from Mouse Brains by Flow Cytometry Using MADM
author: Amberg, Cheung, et al.

steps.title: Generate experimental MADM mice
steps.instruction: Cross MADMTG/TG,gene‑X mice with MADMGT/GT;Nestin‑Cre mice, monitor vaginal plug, use F1 males/females (genotype control MADMGT/TG;Nestin‑Cre or mosaic MADMGT/TG,gene‑X;Nestin‑Cre), and perform experiments at the chosen developmental stage (embryonic to >P21, optimal embryonic‑to‑P0). Timing: 12–80 days.

substeps.instruction: Set up breeding cross: MADMTG/TG,gene‑X × MADMGT/GT;Nestin‑Cre.
Check for vaginal plug to confirm successful mating.
Use F1 generation males and females for experiments (genotype as above).
Select developmental stage(s) for analysis (embryonic, P0, early postnatal, or adult >P21).

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Dissect MADM‑labeled mouse brains and generate a single‑cell suspension suitable for flow sorting. Timing: 1.5–3 h.

steps.title: Set up flow cytometer for sorting
steps.instruction: Configure the sorter, prepare RNase‑treated tubes, and flush the system before loading the sample. Sorting duration: 45 min to 3 h.

substeps.instruction: Install a 100 µm nozzle.
Turn on the 488 nm and 561 nm lasers.
Set sample and collection‑tube temperature to 4 °C.
Prepare one FACS tube with RNase Away and one with RNase‑free water.
Flush each solution through the system for ~1 min (first RNase Away, then RNase‑free water).

steps.title: Filter and dilute cell suspension
steps.instruction: Remove debris, dilute the suspension, and insert test sort tubes.

substeps.instruction: Filter the entire sample through a 40 µm cell strainer using a P1000 pipette with filter tips.
Dilute the filtered sample with 200–300 µL media while pipetting through the strainer.
Insert test‑sort collection tubes (empty 1.5 mL microfuge tubes or empty 0.2 mL PCR tubes).
For BD Aria only: use the test sort to adjust side streams, then discard the test tubes. (SONY side streams cannot be adjusted by the operator.)

steps.title: Configure cytometer parameters and acquire events
steps.instruction: Select detection parameters, optimise gain, and record events for gating.

substeps.instruction: For SONY SH800, select FSC‑A, FSC‑H, FSC‑W, BSC‑A, BSC‑H, BSC‑W, GFP, and tdT.
For BD Aria, select FSC‑A, FSC‑H, FSC‑W, SSC‑A, SSC‑H, SSC‑W, FITC, and mCherry.
Optimise sensor gain according to signal strength.
Load the sample and record 30 000–50 000 events to establish gating.
Define negative fluorescence by setting the voltage so the negative‑population peak maximum is at 102.
Switch axis display to biexponential for inclusive visualization of all events.
Perform manual compensation on SONY (drag populations to correct direction); BD Aria does not require compensation.

steps.title: Prepare collection tubes for downstream analysis
steps.instruction: Set up appropriate tubes and buffers for low‑input RNA‑seq, 10X scRNA‑seq, or proteomics.

substeps.instruction: Low‑input bulk RNA‑seq: fill 0.2 mL PCR tubes with 4 µL lysis buffer. Create a custom holder by cutting the lid off a 1.5 mL microfuge tube, filling it with paper tissue, and inserting the PCR tube.
10X Genomics scRNA‑seq: fill 1.5 mL microfuge tubes with 100 µL media.
Proteomics: fill 1.5 mL microfuge tubes with 50 µL LYSE‑NHS lysis buffer (PreOmics iST‑NHS kit).

steps.title: Set sorting layout and assign gates
steps.instruction: Choose the appropriate tube holder, apply the gating strategy, and start the sort.

substeps.instruction: For SONY, select the 2‑way tube holder in the software wizard.
For BD Aria, open “Sort layout” in BD DIVA, choose a 4‑tube collection device, and select 4‑way purity mode.

Assign gates: debris/live discrimination, doublet exclusion (FSC‑A vs FSC‑W, then SSC‑H/SSC‑W or BSC‑H/BSC‑W), and GFP/tdT (or FITC/mCherry) gates for MADM+ populations (GFP+, tdT+, and optionally GFP+ tdT+ double‑positive).
Start sorting, setting either a maximum number of labeled cells to collect or allowing indefinite collection.

steps.title: Record output and handle bulk RNA‑seq samples
steps.instruction: Document sorted cell numbers and transfer RNA‑seq samples to a 96‑well plate.

substeps.instruction: Note the number of sorted cells for each population (BD Aria records this automatically; SONY does not).
For bulk RNA‑seq, transfer the entire collected volume into an empty well of a 96‑well plate, keep the plate on dry ice, and pipette quickly to avoid freezing in the tip.
Design the plate layout, including a positive‑control well (up to 400 cells) if desired, and consult the sequencing facility about layout requirements.

steps.title: Collect and store RNA samples in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Gather all replicates in a single 96‑well plate, store at –80 °C, and keep on dry ice during handling.

substeps.instruction: Fill the plate with all replicates in one day or add samples over multiple days.
If adding over days/weeks, store the plate at –80 °C until all samples are collected.

steps.title: Seal, freeze, and store plate for sequencing
steps.instruction: Seal the plate, freeze it, and store under conditions suitable for downstream applications.

substeps.instruction: Seal the plate with AluminaSeal.
Freeze immediately on dry ice and store at –80 °C.
Process plates within three months for optimal sequencing efficiency.
For 10X Genomics: spin down tubes, remove supernatant, resuspend pellet in Chromium Next GEM Master Mix, and follow the 10X protocol.
For proteomics: boil samples for 10 min, then continue with the iST‑NHS kit (PreOmics).

steps.title: Critical considerations for sample preparation
steps.instruction: Plan sorting and suspension preparation to maximise cell viability.

substeps.instruction: Only one sample can be sorted at a time; determine required cell numbers beforehand.
Minimise time on ice before sorting to reduce dead‑cell proportion.
Prepare single‑cell suspensions in multiple batches rather than a single large batch to keep individual samples on ice for a short period.
